This document lists the equipment inspection I1, to be performed every five 
years as indicated by Y5 in the title block
Safety valves for the drum & Hot Reheat function: to protect from over pressure.

items: A work permit must be issued and the maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category.

Safety fence with caution marks must 
 be surrounding 
 the work area is required.

Wear the 
 safety 
 and healthy equipment as safety helmet, safety shoes, ...etc).

Hearing and eye protection should be used when working on a valve which is 
 under pressure.
The boiler must be drained, and the boiler vents must be opend .
Never strike a valve which is under pressure premature actuation can result .

Never stand in front of the discharge out let of pressure relief valve which 
 is under pressure.

Always take a great care when you approach 
 or use any pressure valve.
Complete maintenance tool set.
Cleaning fluid, manual puller.
Suitable lifting device feeler gauge .
Hammer air wrench.
Check the safety valves for external leakage ( See annex 1= Fig 1.2 ).
Check the safety valves internal leakage.
Check the adjusting ring set screw.
Check the forked level for damage.
Check spring for any damage

Check the setting pressure by using the air set device (it makes with boiler 
 in operation).

On low and medium pressure drum valves the bonnet and spring can be lifted up 
 over the spindle.

Nearly all super heater valves have cooling spools ans also deflector collars 
 on the spindles. It is not necessary to break the joint between the bonnet and 
 the cooling spool. It will, however, be necessary to remove the deflector 
 collar locking device enough to let the collar move freely up and down the 
 spindle. The bonnet, cooling spool and spring can then be lifted up over the 
 spindle

When applicable, Safety valve seats may be lapped to a micro inch finish using 
 special compounds. Prior to supper-finishing the valve seats should be lapped 
 flat and to a fine surface finish in accordance with standard practice as 
 specified above .

The diamond lapping compound PDH-6 is used in conjuction with a lapping and 
 cleaning thinner PDH-27 and should be used as described in the following 
 procedure .

Clean lapping block using varsol, Acetone or apply cleaning thinner PSH-27, 
 then with a clean dry lint-free cloth or cotton prior to applying lapping 
 compount

Apply dots of PDH-6 on the lapping block approximately to 1 inch apart (not 
 less than four (4) per block ), circumferentially on the face of the lapping 
 block and then apply a drop of lapping thinner PDH-27 to each dot of compound 
 .

Lap the valve seat, keeping the lapping block against the seat and applying 
 slight downward pressure. During the operation the lapping compound may begin 
 to get stiff and movement of the lapping block more difficult; remove lap from 
 lapped surface and add a few drops of lapping thinner PDH-27 to the lapping 
 block, replace on surface being lapped and continue to rotate exerting no 
 downward pressure.

Before a valve is assembled all parts and bearings (fig. 6) should be 
 thoroughly cleaned. This is usually done with emery cloth and wibed clean with 
 a reg. By this method, all foreign matter that might cause leakage or faulty 
 action is removed. If valves are to be assembled without retesting, care must 
 be taken not to mix the parts of different valves. figure 7

When all the parts, guide, contact surfaces and bearings have been cleaned, 
 the seats properly reconditioned and all lapping compound removed, the valve 
 is ready to be assembled. This is done as follows :

Screw the nozzle ring on the nozzle, making certain that it is below the top 
 surface of the nozzle seat. If the former position is known, return the 
 ring to it, otherwise blow down adjustment. figure 8: "nozzle ring setting"

Wipe the nozzle (3) and disc seats (6,7) clean with a cloth and then place the 
 guide, guide ring (10) disc and spindle assembly in the valve bode. Be sure 
 that the guide ring, is in the same position as when the valve was dismantled 
 .

Carefully lower the bonnet (17) and spring (20) into place, using care not to 
 damage the seats or spindle. Then center the bonnet (17) and tighten it down 
 evenly, to prevent any unnecessary strains or possible misalignment of the 
 parts .

Before applying any load to the spring rotate it rapidly to be sure that the 
 spindle is free, it should rotate freely with the spring. If it does not, the 
 cooling spool or the bonnet, or both should be shifted until any binding 
 disappears .

The adjusting bolt is now tightened until the distance between the prick punch 
 marks on the bolt and the machined surface on the bonnet top is the same as 
 before the valve was dismantled. Unless considerable lapping or machining has 
 been done the set pressure should be almost the same as before reconditioning. 
 Correction can be made for metal removed by machining .

Tighten the guide (adj) and nozzle ring setscrews and if the valve is to be 
 tested and adjusted on the boiler, refer to instructions
